items.note: Bhoja's victory over Bhīma is described by the Udayapur praśasti.
Udayapur praśasti gives a general description of Bhoja's victory over the Caulukya king, though no direct evidence that he wrested Abu back.
Assessment: Bhoja admittedly a king of superior merit and rare valour, a military leader of a high order.
Bhoja's arm felt by Karṇāṭas, Śilāhāras, Cedis and Caulukyas; his soldiers marched through Kanauj and Ajmer.
Schools established, bounties for scholars; Bhoja himself a great poet beloved by literary men.
Udayapur praśasti credits Bhoja with building a large number of temples; few remains survive as many were converted into mosques after the Moslem conquest.
Bhoja died during the war with Kalacuris and Caulukyas; enemies captured Dhārā; successor Jayasimha lacked resources.
Someśvara's son Vikramāditya routed Karṇa and Bhīma and restored Jayasimha; Paramāra government reasserted itself, bereft of pristine glory.
Mandhata plates of 1055 A.D. issued from Dhāra: Jayasimha grants a village for Brahmans of the pattāsālā at Amareśvara.
